name: Brainstormzz
shortDescription: Full-stack AI platform converting unstructured input into hierarchical visual maps.
problem: Founders and engineers struggle to transform raw, unstructured thoughts into organized, actionable project roadmaps without tedious manual diagramming.
whyBuilt: Built to provide founders and builders with an intelligent whiteboard workspace that instantly structures brain dumps into hierarchical, visual thought maps.
contribution: Architected full-stack application, integrated OpenAI API prompt-to-JSON schemas, built interactive visual canvas, and conducted user research with 12 early-stage founders.
challenges: Engineering deterministic, strictly formatted hierarchical JSON trees from diverse natural language prompts while maintaining sub-second canvas rendering.
lessonsLearned: Discovered advanced JSON schema steering via OpenAI API, client-side canvas tree traversal optimizations, and early feedback collection workflows.
futureImprovements: Add real-time multiplayer cursor collaboration and native markdown export integrations.
metrics: 50+ beta users onboarded within 2 weeks of launch • 98% successful generation rate • 12 early-stage founders consulted in user research

name: Urban Carpool Matching System
shortDescription: Route optimization algorithm matching drivers and riders across regional zones with multi-constraint logic.
problem: Urban commuters encounter inefficient transit and high gas expenses due to low occupancy vehicles and lack of automated constraint-satisfaction ride matching.
whyBuilt: Designed to calculate optimal driver-rider pairings considering pickup proximity, time schedules, and detours to reduce commute distance.
contribution: Engineered route matching graph algorithm in Python with constraint satisfaction logic, geofenced zone partitioning, and distance cost evaluation.
challenges: Optimizing combinatorial matching complexity across high-density regional pickup zones while enforcing maximum allowable detour thresholds.
lessonsLearned: Implemented heuristic clustering to divide regional zones, significantly accelerating matching throughput without compromising route efficiency.
futureImprovements: Integrate real-time GTFS transit feed comparisons and a React web dashboard.
metrics: 100+ drivers/riders matched across 15 regional zones • 22% average commute distance reduction

name: Rover Arm Controller & CV Test Automation
shortDescription: Socket-based robotic arm control system with a computer vision test automation framework validating ARUCO tags.
problem: Robotic rover arms need reliable low-latency control and rigorous automated visual test suites to prevent mechanical collisions in unfamiliar terrain.
whyBuilt: Built to bridge software commanding with microcontroller hardware actuators and automate precision validation using computer vision.
contribution: Developed TCP/UDP socket communication protocol connecting Python host control to Arduino microcontrollers, alongside an OpenCV test automation suite.
challenges: Synchronizing asynchronous socket packet transmission with physical stepper motor timing while maintaining accurate ARUCO marker pose estimation.
lessonsLearned: Learned packet serialization protocols, hardware edge timing boundaries, and robust image thresholding under variable lighting conditions.
futureImprovements: Add inverse kinematics calculation engine and depth-camera point cloud obstacle avoidance.
metrics: 100+ test scenarios executed • 15+ firmware & vision defects identified and resolved

name: 8-Bit General-Purpose Processor
shortDescription: 8-bit processor designed in VHDL with an ALU, FSM control unit, decoder, and registers, validated on FPGA.
problem: Understanding modern computing systems requires mastering digital hardware abstractions—from logic gates to register-transfer level microarchitectures.
whyBuilt: Designed and synthesized a functional 8-bit general-purpose CPU from fundamental digital circuits up to FPGA physical verification.
contribution: Designed the arithmetic logic unit (ALU), finite state machine (FSM) control unit, instruction decoder, registers, and multiplexed seven-segment display controller in VHDL.
challenges: Managing clock domain timing hazards and coordinating microcode state sequencing across memory fetch, decode, execute, and writeback stages.
lessonsLearned: Deepened mastery of RTL design, timing closure, propagation delays, setup/hold constraints, and hardware testbench waveform analysis.
futureImprovements: Expand register file to 16-bit and implement a pipelined execution architecture.
metrics: 100% match between simulated waveforms and FPGA hardware execution across all instruction sets

name: Bookstore Management Application
shortDescription: Java Swing bookstore system with Owner/Customer workflows, persistent storage, and State Pattern membership.
problem: Retail store operators require streamlined software separating inventory operations from customer purchases with dynamic rewards tier management.
whyBuilt: Developed as an object-oriented software engineering system applying design patterns to manage persistent catalog inventory, customer balances, and tier discounts.
contribution: Architected complete system using Java Swing GUI, encapsulated persistent file I/O storage, and implemented the State Design Pattern for Gold/Silver member tiers.
challenges: Decoupling role-based workflow interfaces while ensuring transactional integrity between customer account points and book stock inventory.
lessonsLearned: Gained practical experience implementing behavioral GoF design patterns (State Pattern) to eliminate nested conditionals in business tier rules.
futureImprovements: Refactor data layer to an embedded SQLite or PostgreSQL database and migrate UI to JavaFX.
metrics: Comprehensive Owner/Customer workflows • Dynamic Gold/Silver membership states • Zero-defect transaction persistence

name: Three-Stage MOSFET Voltage Amplifier
shortDescription: Two active-load common-source gain stages plus common-drain buffer in 180nm CMOS technology.
problem: High-frequency analog signal processing requires amplifiers with elevated voltage gain, wide bandwidth, low output impedance, and stable bias points.
whyBuilt: Designed and simulated an analog integrated circuit meeting strict gain, bandwidth, power, voltage swing, and input/output impedance criteria.
contribution: Calculated device dimensions (W/L) for 180nm CMOS technology, performed DC bias, AC frequency response, and transient simulation sweeps in ngspice and KiCad.
challenges: Balancing gain-bandwidth trade-offs and output voltage swing against saturation margin across process corners.
lessonsLearned: Mastered small-signal analysis, Miller effect compensation, active current mirror load biasing, and simulation-based circuit characterization.
futureImprovements: Perform full layout, parasitic extraction, and corner variation analysis.
metrics: Met 100% of target specs — gain, bandwidth, power consumption, dynamic swing, and load sensitivity
